subject: Information Theory
title: Parity Bits
description: A quick, practical guide to Parity Bits.

hook.text: Add one extra bit to make the total number of 1s even. If the count comes out odd, something flipped.

buildup.text: A parity bit is the simplest error detection: one bit of redundancy catches any single-bit error.

discovery.text: Even parity: count the 1s, add a bit so the total is even. Odd parity works the same way but targets odd totals.

twist.text: Parity detects single errors but can't correct them. And two errors cancel out—parity sees nothing.

climax.text: Despite its limits, parity is used in RAM (ECC memory), serial communication, and RAID storage.

punchline.text: One extra bit. Catches one error. Misses two.

quiz.question: What is the main limitation of a single parity bit?
options: It detects but cannot correct errors, and misses double errors
